highlights.title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
highlights.summary: Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout.
body: The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters. Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported.

But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal.

TSMC’s chip fabrication plants physically produce the vast majority of Nvidia’s chips designed for AI data center workloads and make most of Apple’s custom chips used in iPhones, Mac laptops and desktops, plus Apple’s planned AI computing server. Most of these fabs are located in Taiwan, but TSMC also operates fabs in Japan and China, and it has an expanding US manufacturing cluster in Arizona. It is also building a new fab in Germany.

highlights.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI
highlights.summary: Radical Numerics has developed a model that it says can identify natural and AI-engineered pathogens without an internet connection.
body: Frontier AI labs have warned that their technology could help develop dangerous bioweapons.

Now, a startup says it has developed a defense. On Wednesday, Radical Numerics announced that it has developed a new edge model called Omnii Defense that is designed to flag natural and AI-engineered pathogens using a laptop and a USB gene sequencer. It can also run without an internet connection, allowing researchers in the field with spotty connections to use it. Though many scientists say AI-made bioweapons are a low-likelihood threat, Radical Numerics hopes its technology will help researchers and public health officials identify emerging biological threats.

Eric Nguyen, cofounder and CEO of Radical Numerics, says he sees a coming arms race in biodefense similar to what’s playing out in cybersecurity, where threat actors and security defenders are leveraging AI in an attempt to gain an edge.
“We felt that the biosecurity space was far behind on the defense side,” he says.

highlights.summary: In an exclusive interview with BBC Radio Shropshire new Shrewsbury Town sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is a perfect fit for the new owners.
body: Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is the perfect project for the US-backed owners after a Europe-wide search ended with them taking contol of the League Two outfit.

Scott Davidson's Biscayne ST LLC consortium, which Friedel is part of, completed their takeover on Monday, buying 87.4% of the shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to relinquish control.
"Scott and I met through friends in Miami and through the love of football and nothing more or less," former Blackburn and USA goalkeeper Friedel told BBC Radio Shropshire in an exclusive interview.
"As we got to know each other, our thoughts on business and football aligned - we got to the point where we said let's try to find a club which fits a whole bunch of criteria.

highlights.title: Blizzard Can't Stop Tweaking WoW: Forever and It's Only Been 6 Days
highlights.summary: While Blizzard has vowed to issue a major balance patch for World of Warcraft: Forever when the retro MMO's raids launch in December, the developer certainly doesn't seem afraid of doing some tinkering under the hood in the meantime. A roundup of hotfixes published on Nov.
body: Perhaps the most notable change is to gold rewards for questing during the higher levels, which have been increased. While many players have yet to reach this stage yet, Blizzard has come under fire for abandoning the conversion of XP into gold once you hit max level — a change applied not long before WoW 's first expansion, The Burning Crusade.

"We felt that it would be inappropriate for WoW: Forever players to be compelled to save up quests as they approach level 60 and then not turn them in until they transformed into a great profit," Blizzard explained. But this has left players at level 60 somewhat cash-strapped.

"In original WoW, only about 25% of quests in the game actually provide raw gold rewards, which led this to be a slightly more negative change than intended to gold income as you get closer to level 60," WoW: Forever 's community manager explained in another post. So Blizzard has added gold rewards to the majority of quests from level 48 onwards. "This change brings high-level quests in-line with the rest of questing in WoW: Forever, with the goal of giving players a good reason to complete those quests while leveling up to 60 and thereafter," Blizzard said.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.summary: Irma P. Hall, who played Josephine “Big Mama” Joseph in the 1997 dramedy “Soul Food,” died on Tuesday, her family confirmed. She was 91. “Irma P. Hall was a beloved actress, author, poet, educator and public speaker whose contributions touched countless lives throughout her remarkable career,” her…
body: Born in Beaumont, Texas, Hall was raised in Chicago before graduating from Texas College in 1956. She became a high school teacher and taught French, Spanish and other languages in Houston and Dallas until she began acting full time in 1984.

Her first role was as Georgia Brown in the independent film “Book of Numbers,” directed by Raymond St. Jacques. She was performing a poem when he scouted her and offered her the role on the spot. She instantly discovered her love for acting. She went on to act in several films and TV shows, including Ron Howard’s action thriller “Backdraft” in 1991 and Peter Macdonald’s comedy-drama “Mo’ Money” in 1992.
Her career continued to grow with “Family Thing,” “Nothing to Lose” and “Steel” before she landed the role of Big Mama.

She received the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture in 1998. “Soul Food” was a hit at the box office, prompting the spinoff series “Soul Food: The Series,” where Hall reprised her role in fantasy sequences.

highlights.title: Loot boxes, influencers, and addictive features face an EU crackdown
highlights.summary: Gaming, social media, and e-commerce platforms are facing a fresh wave of sweeping European Union rules that aim to make "your online experience fairer." The newly proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA) published by the EU Commission on Wednesday is designed to tackle practices that exploit consumers…
body: The proposed Digital Fairness Act seeks to bolster consumer protections for online users.

“The Act will protect consumers of all ages shopping and browsing for goods or services online,” the EU Commission said in a news bulletin. “It will also mean fairer competition for businesses, which are expecting to save EU consumers up to €13.7 billion ($15.1 billion) a year.”

The scope of the restrictions being proposed is broad, and could have a significant impact on major parts of the online digital landscape, from the “rabbit hole” algorithms across YouTube, TikTok, and Meta platforms, to AI chatbots and apps like DuoLingo that relentlessly nudge users to keep interacting with them. Some gaming organizations have already slammed the DFA proposal, describing its restrictions around virtual currencies, loot boxes, and offering micro-transactions to minors as being “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate.”

body: Grahame Morris, the Labour MP for Easington, submitted a parliamentary motion on Tuesday urging the government to take action to reduce the number of times a player can head the ball in training.
Researchers have found footballers are three and a half times more likely to die from a neurodegenerative disease than the general population.
The Early Day Motion (EDM) describes the need to protect players' brain health as a "significant public health and player welfare issue".

"The aim of this EDM is to raise awareness of the growing body of evidence linking repeated head impacts, particularly from heading a football, to an increased risk of neurodegenerative disease," Morris told BBC Sport.

highlights.summary: "We're not making mobile games this time," says former Hutch boss Shaun Rutland.
body: The founding team behind Top Drives and F1 Clash developer Hutch has raised $5m to build a new company focused on interactive generative video.
Anorak’s pre-seed round was co-led by Play Ventures and Backed VC, with Supercell and MTG also taking part. Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron is among the angel investors.

The startup is led by CEO Shaun Rutland, who co-founded Hutch before MTG acquired it for $375m in 2020, and chief creative officer Jonathan Alpine, who held the same role at Hutch. David Amor is COO, and cofounder Tak Fung runs the company’s AI lab in Chengdu, China. Anorak now has a team of 20 across London and Chengdu.
As we reported last week, Rutland has been teasing Anorak through his blog, describing it as a studio focused on “interactive generative video”.

body: The first surprise of the Geese live experience is Green’s swagger and experimentation. The guitarist is a key player in guiding the band’s more experimental moments and ferocious improvisation. Often tinkering with pedals as her fingers fly across the fretboard, she’s able to stretch a song to the outer limits, only to snap back quickly and clearly when a sharp riff is called for. Bassin also is central to the style, furiously playing all over his kit while still keeping in the pocket, ready to let loose during solos on songs such as the jumpy kiss-off “Bow Down.” DiGesu’s bass was often the steadiest instrument of the night, deep and powerful despite flights of fancy from his bandmates.

highlights.title: Trump admin loses fight to spy on random journalists’ LinkedIn DMs
highlights.summary: The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday.
body: The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted.

highlights.title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
highlights.summary: Predicting how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types and disease.
body: Our next-generation DNA sequence model bridges single-cell biology and human genetics, predicting how genetic variants affect hundreds of human cell types.

Today, we are announcing AlphaGenome 2, our next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types, giving scientists a powerful new tool to uncover the cellular drivers of disease.

Cells are the building blocks of life. Every cell in our body carries the same DNA blueprint, yet each cell type and state—like a heart muscle cell or an immune cell fighting an infection—switches different genes on or off to do its job. Global efforts like the Human Cell Atlas are mapping this gene expression for millions of cells, but it is still an unsolved challenge to predict how subtle DNA variations affect this expression in cells, which is a key driver of human traits and disease.

highlights.summary: Former Jets and Bills coach turned himself in. Ryan faces six misdemeanor charges over incident. Two pedestrians allegedly struck in Nashville. ESPN analyst and former NFL coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to police on Wednesday after allegedly hitting two pedestrians with his car in Nashville and…
body: Nashville police said on Wednesday that the pedestrians had the right of way while crossing a main street in the city’s downtown last week when Ryan allegedly turned at a red light and drove over their feet.

Ryan was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failing to provide information or render aid and two counts of failing to obey a traffic control signal, according to court records. All six charges are misdemeanors.

Ryan, 63, served as head coach of the New York Jets from 2009 to 2014 and the Buffalo Bills from 2015 to 2016. He led the Jets to consecutive AFC championship games following the 2009 and 2010 seasons.
His father, the late Buddy Ryan, was a celebrated NFL coach who served as defensive coordinator of the 1985 Chicago Bears, whose defense is widely regarded as one of the greatest in league history.

highlights.title: Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum Officially Wraps Filming
highlights.summary: We are one step closer to seeing a new Lord of the Rings film in theaters. Andy Serkis has confirmed that principal photography on The Hunt for Gollum has been completed, which he is directing in addition to reprising the titular role that made him famous.
body: Serkis broke the news during an interview on The Morning Mosh Pit, adding that he won't say too much about the film right now, because promoting it will be his focus all of next year. He did say that making The Hunt for Gollum has been "an incredible journey," which feels apt for a Lord of the Rings film. Jamie Dornan, who will take over the role of Aragorn from Viggo Mortensen for the film, similarly revealed to Variety that he had finished shooting his scenes about three weeks ago.

Dornan is an interesting part of The Hunt for Gollum, as one of the only actors stepping into a role played by someone else in Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy. In addition to Serkis, both Elijah Wood and Ian McKellen are returning for the film to reprise their roles as Frodo Baggins and Gandalf, respectively. They'll all be joined by several newcomers playing original characters we haven't seen in live-action before, such as Kate Winslet as Marigol, Leo Woodall as Halvard, and Anya Taylor-Joy as Seren. The film is going to be something of an interquel to The Fellowship of the Ring, following Aragorn as Gandfalf sends him to capture Gollum to gain information on the One Ring.

highlights.title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
highlights.summary: The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players.
body: This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance “declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity.”

Noting “a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools,” the group of jurors called out AI’s ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still “not a foregone conclusion in our industry.”
The jurors also urged the IGF as a whole to “adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work.”

highlights.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
highlights.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease - and point the way to new treatments.
body: DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment.

AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year. While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells — from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection — switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change depending on what a cell is doing. As a result, the same genetic variant can have very different effects depending on the type and state of the cell.

The new model is designed to capture those differences, predicting the effects of genetic variants on individual cell types and states. Google said in a blog post published Wednesday that it offers a much finer-grained view than broader models like AlphaGenome, potentially revealing disease-relevant effects in specific cells that might otherwise go unnoticed.

"He wanted it. He wanted to feel like the pressure was on him and the responsibility was on him to produce for the team. He enjoyed that. You always saw the best of Josh when the ante was up. I never once saw him not deliver in those circumstances.

"We would play tournaments in France, Spain and Portugal, against the giants of Europe, and afterwards the staff from each club would have to pick the best player they'd seen across the weekend. I remember Josh winning that accolade more than once."

King's temperament now forms part of his appeal to Thomas Tuchel, who called him up for England ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden. "It's the attitude and the personality," he said last week. It all bodes well ahead of a possible debut against Croatia or Spain.

highlights.title: GTA 6 might be censored in Japan, if the game's smaller install size and lack of "strong sexual content" warning is anything to go by
highlights.summary: GTA 6 is finally coming out worldwide next week, putting an end to a 13-year wait and at least one popular meme format, but the highly-anticipated game might look a bit different in Japan.
body: Now that pre-loading is live for the Rockstar Games mammoth, players across the globe can finally download the game and drool over its icon for the next week or so. But pre-orderers in Japan have noticed that GTA 6's file size comes to about 208GB on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores, versus up to 212GB in other regions.

As reported on by GameSpark and covered by Automaton, the game also received the strictest age rating from the Japanese certification board CERO - "Z" which is recommended for players aged 18 and over - but the listing notably doesn't contain one disclaimer seen in other international ratings.

PEGI and ESRB both warn of the game's "strong sexual content." Curiously, CERO's rating includes no such disclaimer. Together, some fans have taken the lack of "sexual content" disclaimer and smaller file size as signs that GTA 6 might not include some of the risque content we know it'll flaunt elsewhere in the world - based on NSFW leaks and a past rating that already clued us into the fact GTA 6 might be the first GTA to feature full-on sex scenes.

highlights.summary: Some of the most impressive tech that Adobe showcases at its annual Max conference each year is the experimental features it's developing, and the latest of those tools are being announced today: they can transform images into explorable 3D scenes, design AI characters by talking to them, and turn…
body: Here are some of the experimental ‘sneaks’ being showcased at Adobe Max.

The first (and weirdest, in my opinion) is Project Screen Test, which is designed to make AI-generated characters easier to develop and use for video content. Instead of just describing how the character should sound and behave in text prompts, the tool lets you talk to the character and direct them in an audition-like environment. You start by describing some base personality traits, such as “anxious, shy, awkward,” and giving the character a voice, either by selecting a preset, describing how it sounds in a prompt, or uploading sample audio for it to reference.

You can then expand its persona in further detail by conversing with the character as if you’re talking on FaceTime, outlining its backstory, temperament, goals, flaws, fears, movement quirks and more. Once you’re happy, the tool lets you generate animated screen tests with the character by describing an environment or scenario you want to put them in.

body: Ethics watchdogs have questioned the necessity of the country’s top diplomat shuttling so often between Washington DC and Gainesville, where his son Anthony has a walk-on role as a running back for the team known as the Gators.

An investigation by the Washington Post found that Rubio has attended at least 10 games in the last two seasons, including five this fall, and that of 23 total trips made to Gainesville on military aircraft, 15 were “personal” in nature.

The newspaper said that while Rubio is prohibited from flying commercially, because of security protocols that also cover the secretary of defense and FBI and CIA directors, his use of government transport “appears to significantly outpace that of his predecessors”.
Using published defense department rates listing the cost per hour of different kinds of military aircraft, the Post calculated that the flights alone have cost more than $1.2m.

And while the cemetery scene unfolding that afternoon is intimate, other sequences have the scale and flamboyance of a classic Hollywood production, notably those recreating the legendary Folies Bergère cabaret in Paris, where Baker became a sensation in the 1920s. highlights.title: Australian supermarket honey taste test: ‘The cheapest honey is still delicious’
highlights.summary: Nicholas Jordan and a hive mind of judges tasted 27 brands of honey and found that while the best were ‘perfumed as hell’, others were as basic as reality TV. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. I’ve bought a lot of honey in my life.
body: I ’ve bought a lot of honey in my life. I purchased kilos of the stuff back when I used to make unmanageably large batches of bootleg muesli. But I don’t think I’ve ever purchased honey and thought about what I’m buying. I couldn’t even name the brands in my cupboard, let alone describe my thought process in choosing them.

I want to be more judicious, but how? All the ingredients are the same. There’s a huge variation in price, and I know from previous taste tests that price is a terrible predictor of deliciousness. So what should I look at? Colour? Branding? Organic certification? Specific botanicals? Where the honey comes from? It’s literally choosing a book by its cover.

I’m about as far as you can get from tech bro optimisation – I get a thrill from hitchhiking, eating unknown ingredients and being yelled at from passing cars. But this level of unpredictability and imprecision makes even me uncomfortable. The difference is, it doesn’t cost any money to be yelled at. Honey comes at a price, and I spent a lot of time acquiring those dollars, so I want to be informed when spending them.
